metadata.summary: Former world No 1 Novak Djokovic won his seventh China Open title without facing a match point in his semi-final and final.
metadata.content: Novak Djokovic: Former world No 1 wins China Open title without facing a match point in semi-final and final | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Breaking Novak Djokovic: Former world No 1 wins China Open title without facing a match point in semi-final and final Novak Djokovic earns his seventh career title in Beijing after Alex De Minaur is forced to retire injured; you can watch the WTA/ATP China Open and ATP 1000 Shanghai Masters live on Sky Sports Tuesday 6 October 2026 13:58, UK Image: Novak Djokovic extends his reign in Beijing with a seventh title Former world No 1 Novak Djokovic won his seventh China Open title without facing a match point in his semi-final and final. Djokovic, who was awarded a win after his semi-final opponent Daniil Medvedev was disqualified after hitting a spectator with the ball , claimed the 102nd title of his career following the retirement of De Minaur in the final 7-6 (7-3) 0-1 on Tuesday. messages.text: Alcaraz wins Japan Open in first final since wrist injury

metadata.summary: Carlos Alcaraz has won his first final since coming back from a long injury lay-off for a right wrist injury with success at the Japan Open.
metadata.content: Carlos Alcaraz: Spaniard wins Japan Open in first final since coming back from injury lay-off for wrist injury | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Carlos Alcaraz: Spaniard wins Japan Open in first final since coming back from injury lay-off for wrist injury Carlos Alcaraz successfully defends Japan Open title in his first final since suffering wrist injury which forced him to miss French Open and Wimbledon; you can watch the ATP 1000 Shanghai Masters live on Sky Sports from Wednesday Tuesday 6 October 2026 13:13, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Carlos Alcaraz against Jiri Lehecka from the Japan Open final Carlos Alcaraz has won his first final since coming back from a long injury lay-off for a right wrist injury with success at the Japan Open. Alcaraz, who hadn't played a showpiece since getting beat by Jannik Sinner at the Monte-Carlo Masters in April successfully defended the title he won last year in Tokyo defeating Jiri Lehecka 7-6 (7-4) 6-4. The Spaniard returned from injury in late August and made a run to the US Open quarter-finals, where he lost to Ben Shelton in a match that ended at 3:33am . messages.text: Russell set for Singapore GP grid penalty after engine failure

metadata.summary: George Russell is set to start from the back of the grid at Sunday's Singapore Grand Prix due to a power unit change in a further blow to his championship hopes.
metadata.content: George Russell: Mercedes driver set to start Singapore GP from back of grid due to penalty caused by Bahrain GP engine failure | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content George Russell: Mercedes driver set to start Singapore GP from back of grid due to penalty caused by Bahrain GP engine failure George Russell suffered an engine failure at the Bahrain GP; the Brit is set to install a new engine that will take him over his quota for the season; watch F1's first ever Singapore Grand Prix Sprint weekend live on Sky Sports F1, with Sprint Qualifying at 1pm on Friday Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Tuesday 6 October 2026 14:11, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell retired in Malaysia with a power unit issue George Russell is set to start from the back of the grid at Sunday's Singapore Grand Prix due to a power unit change in a further blow to his championship hopes. Russell suffered a power unit failure late in Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia when running third, forcing him to retire while his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli finished second to extend his lead over the Brit at the top of the Drivers' Championship to 84 points with seven rounds remaining. Sky Sports News understands Russell will take on a new power unit on Friday in Singapore, which will see him exceed the season allocation of four for each driver, therefore incurring a penalty that will drop him to the rear of the grid. metadata.content: Jannik Sinner: World No 1 to miss rest of season due to knee injury and has not played since winning Wimbledon | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Jannik Sinner: World No 1 to miss rest of season due to knee injury and has not played since winning Wimbledon Jannik Sinner will not return to the court until 2027; Italian's last match was victory over Alexander Zverev in Wimbledon final in July; five-time Grand Slam champion could lose No 1 ranking before end of season with Zverev pushing for that spot; watch tennis live on Sky Sports Tuesday 6 October 2026 10:54, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports commentator Liam Broady says it is a blow to the game that Jannik Sinner's 2026 season has ended prematurely World No 1 ‌Jannik Sinner will miss the rest of the 2026 season due to the knee injury that has kept him on the sidelines since winning Wimbledon. metadata.summary: The headset goes on and I am transported from a central London meeting room to the centre circle of a match simulation. I have selected the role of holding midfielder. I grip a controller in each hand, thumb hovering over the pass button.
metadata.content: Scanning offers players like Martin Odegaard an edge as football becomes faster and more intense | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Scanning offers players like Martin Odegaard an edge as football becomes faster and more intense Sky Sports' Nick Wright tried out virtual reality technology designed to train scanning to see how some players are improving their off-the-ball awareness; Martin Odegaard, Aurelien Tchouameni, Marc Guehi and Romeo Lavia are among those to have used it Nick Wright Football Features Writer @nicholaspwright Tuesday 6 October 2026 13:23, UK Image: Martin Odegaard, Aurelien Tchouameni and Romeo Lavia have used virtual reality technology to improve their scanning The headset goes on and I am transported from a central London meeting room to the centre circle of a match simulation. I have selected the role of holding midfielder. I grip a controller in each hand, thumb hovering over the pass button. After a short countdown, a passage of build-up play begins at the feet of a virtual team-mate. My task is to receive the ball and choose the appropriate pass, all while every movement of my head, and every subsequent decision, is logged and analysed. The technology, created by Be Your Best , is designed to train scanning, those little glances from side to side made by players to gather information about their surroundings which can be used to inform their decisions when they receive the ball. messages.text: 'Painful as hell' - Norris uncertain McLaren can fix issue for Singapore

metadata.summary: Lando Norris has admitted he is unsure whether McLaren will be able to fix an issue with his car that is causing a loss of straight-line speed ahead of this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Lando Norris uncertain McLaren can fix 'painful' straight-line speed issue ahead of Singapore Grand Prix | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Lando Norris uncertain McLaren can fix 'painful' straight-line speed issue ahead of Singapore Grand Prix Lando Norris has endured disappointing weekends in Azerbaijan and Malaysia, with a straight-line speed issue frustrating the British driver; watch F1's first ever Singapore Grand Prix Sprint weekend live on Sky Sports F1, with Sprint Qualifying at 1pm on Friday Tuesday 6 October 2026 09:05, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia at the Sepang International Circuit. Lando Norris has admitted he is unsure whether McLaren will be able to fix an issue with his car that is causing a loss of straight-line speed ahead of this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix. The reigning world champion was in fine form as he claimed three pole positions and two victories in four races spread either side of the summer break, but he has since been off the pace in Azerbaijan and Malaysia. Norris only qualified fifth at both events, was taken out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in a crash and could only manage ninth in an error-strewn display as Malaysia hosted the Bahrain Grand Prix. metadata.content: Harmanpreet Kaur: India's World Cup-winning captain steps down from role across all three formats of cricket | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Harmanpreet Kaur: India's World Cup-winning captain steps down from role across all three formats of cricket Harmanpreet Kaur led India to first-ever global women's cricket title on home soil in 2025 as they beat South Africa in the 50-over World Cup final; batter, 37, says she has given "everything" to India while captaining in five Tests, 51 one-day internationals and 155 T20 internationals Tuesday 6 October 2026 09:15, UK Image: Harmanpreet Kaur captained India to victory at the 2025 50-over World Cup - the women's team's first global trophy India's World Cup-winning captain Harmanpreet Kaur has stepped down from the role across all three formats. The batter, 37, led India to their first-ever global women's title at the 2025 50-over World Cup on home soil. Harmanpreet is only the third Indian captain, after men's players Kapil Dev and MS Dhoni, to guide a team to victory in that event.
